Groundwater forecasting · Bengaluru

Know how deep a well's water will be, weeks before it gets there.

Many homes and businesses in Bengaluru depend on borewells. Their water level rises with the monsoon, falls with pumping, and a well can run low with little warning. We built a proof of concept that turns routine pump records into forecasts for each well, with an honest range around every forecast.

What we built

Three capabilities, each tested against answers the model was not allowed to see in advance.

A forecast for every well

For each of the ~500 wells we monitor: where its water is now, and where it is likely to be in 4, 8 and 12 weeks, with a range.

Try it →

What moves the water

How much the monsoon lifts a well, how much pumping pulls it down, and how long rain takes to reach the groundwater.

How wells affect each other

A simulation showing which wells' pumping hurts their neighbours most, and what it would take to measure that for real.

Where the data comes from

We are careful to say which results come from real wells and which come from simulations. Each result on this site carries one of these labels.

Real pump data

15 days, 579 real wells

A real export of pump sessions and water levels from July 2026. Enough to build and check the method, too short to forecast months ahead.

Synthetic test system

450 simulated wells, known answers

A test system where the true water level is known, so we could check which methods recover it and what data they need.

Digital twin

A full year for all 579 wells

A physics-based simulation of the same wells over a year, including the monsoon. It stands in for the long real history we are requesting.

How we got here

Each stage answered one question and set up the next.

STAGE 1

Can pump records become forecasts?

Yes: 15 days of real data were cleaned, linked and modelled.

 STAGE 2

What matters most: data or model?

Data. Resting-level readings cut error from 4.2 m to 0.5 m on a test system.

 STAGE 3

How far ahead can we see?

Twelve weeks, at half the error of guessing, with honest ranges.

 STAGE 4

Do wells affect each other?

In simulation, yes. We know what data would measure it.

Read the full journey What we need next

Honest status

This is a proof of concept. The long-range results come from a digital twin and a synthetic test system, not yet from years of real field records. The next step is to repeat these tests on real long-term data. Here is what that needs.

Borewell Forecast is a proof of concept for forecasting groundwater levels in Bengaluru borewells. Results are labelled by where the data came from: real pump data (15 days, July 2026), synthetic test system (450 simulated wells with a known answer) or digital twin (a physics-based simulation of the 579 wells over a year). Nothing here is yet a validated field forecast.
